digest.component_or_area: bridge reconciler library and MCP surfaces
propositions: Extract a typed result-bearing classification helper beneath run_pass() that returns disposition and structured pass detail before _finish_disposition() collapses to integer exit code, reusing the canonical in-process route classification seam for both CLI and library/MCP adapters.

Expose new public library functions (bridge_preview, bridge_sync, bridge_status, bridge_pause, bridge_resume, bridge_check_access) with explicit typed inputs and outputs, reusing the shared core reconciler without duplicating mode or exit-code tables.

Register new MCP tools paralleling the machine-usable bridge operations with explicit typed inputs, no mode parameter, and published outputSchemas; gate every mutating route through mcp.allow_jira_sync while preserving read-only access.

Preserve legacy rebar.reconcile(mode=...) and bridge_fsck() exports with unchanged signatures, defaults, return values, exceptions, and mutation boundaries through compatibility adapters that normalize into the shared semantic route.

Maintain identical semantic state and mutation outcomes between legacy library/MCP reconcile modes and their mapped new bridge operations, validated through cross-surface compatibility tests comparing CLI, library, and MCP dispositions.

Update documentation to present noun-based bridge operations as primary while explicitly documenting retained legacy entrypoints as supported compatibility contracts with no forced immediate migration.
